newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU failure would be crisis for France - de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU failure would be crisis for France - de Silguy.

text.p: Failure to launch European Economic and Monetary Union in 1999 would be a catastrophe for France, European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said in a newspaper interview published on Thursday.

"I think the 1999 date is inevitable. Failure to respect it would lead to such a crisis for our country and our economy that I cannot imagine this catastrophic scenario," the Frenchman said in an interview with daily Le Figaro.
He said the drive towards a single European currency was unpopular in France because it was being used as a scapegoat for weak growth and high unemployment.
Even without EMU, France needed to cut its budget deficit. And it required structural reforms to reduce unemployment, currently at a record 12.6 percent.
He argued the European single market would not survive if it were forced to undergo the kind of currency instability it had suffered from between 1992 and 1995.

De Silguy, who was adviser to former prime minister Edouard Balladur, said the scars of a 1992 French referendum on EMU had still not healed fully. French people voted very narrowly in favour of EMU in the referendum.
De Silguy, responding to a call by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for a sharp depreciation in the franc, also said the franc was not overvalued compared to the mark.
"From 1987 to 1995 French competitiveness in terms of unit labour costs improved four percent compared to other partners in the European Monetary System.
"If the franc were overvalued, markets would end up drawing the consequences of that," he said.
